body:
BOTH BINDING ROUND-3 REQUIREMENTS ARE SATISFIED. I am stating that first and unambiguously, because the prior verdict named them without quoting them and you should not have to wonder whether they are still open. They are not.

  R1 marker constant + coupling test   IMPLEMENTER_APPROACH_MARKER at lib.rs:77000;
                                       extract_implementer_approach now reads it;
                                       pickup_template_and_reader_share_one_marker
                                       include_str!s the MASTER template and asserts
                                       it contains the constant. Both directions fail
                                       as required: edit the template heading and the
                                       test goes red, edit the constant and it goes
                                       red too. Reading the master rather than the
                                       scaffolded copy is the right choice and the
                                       reason you gave for it is correct.
  R2 absence note + end-to-end test    append_implementer_approach emits the section
                                       with "_None recorded._" instead of nothing;
                                       generate_review_prompt_carries_the_approach_
                                       and_says_so_when_absent drives the REAL
                                       generator through a temp store and asserts
                                       both arms - present carries widget.rs and is
                                       NOT "_None recorded._", absent has the heading
                                       and IS. That is the seam the helper-only tests
                                       could not see, tested at the seam.

ONE NEW FINDING, INTRODUCED BY THIS COMMIT, AND IT IS THE COMMIT'S OWN SUBJECT.

    lib.rs:77000   pub(crate) const IMPLEMENTER_APPROACH_MARKER = "## Implementer approach"
    lib.rs:77032   "...did not leave a comment beginning `## Implementer approach`, so
                    this review has no stated intent to check the diff against."

The absence message HARD-CODES THE MARKER AS A LITERAL, thirty-two lines below the constant that exists to stop exactly that. Three instances of the string now live in production paths where there were two, and the new one was added by the change whose purpose is coupling them.

WHY IT IS WORSE THAN THE DEFECT IT REPLACES, not merely untidy. Rename the constant tomorrow and: the parser follows it, the template is caught by your coupling test and forces the edit - and THE MESSAGE STILL TELLS THE HUMAN TO WRITE THE OLD HEADING. The system would then parse for X while instructing reviewers to write Y. The original defect had both sides agreeing and silently not matching; this one has them disagreeing in the instructions, which is the state where a human follows the prompt and is wrong. Your own constant doc says the failure is invisible "precisely because both sides still work" - this adds a third side that does not even have a test.

THE COUPLING TEST DOES NOT COVER IT. It asserts template contains constant. Nothing asserts the message does. So the guard this commit adds is blind to the instance this commit adds.

REMEDY AS THE SEAM: no production string names the marker except the constant - a `format!` with `{IMPLEMENTER_APPROACH_MARKER}` is the whole fix. I would NOT extend the coupling test to grep the message; make it structurally impossible instead, which is what the constant is for.

DELIBERATELY NOT A FINDING - the test-file literals at story_1350_review_approach_tests.rs:11, 14, 26 and 95. Those are FIXTURES, and a fixture that builds its input from the constant cannot detect a change to the constant. Literal is correct there. I checked them rather than pattern-matching on "the string appears again".

MERGE-READINESS, separate predicate: NOT MERGEABLE. Build (ubuntu-latest) pending at eb35c424f36d, merge-hold label present so merge-hold-gate fails by design. Independent of this verdict in both directions.

NOTE ON THE RECORD ITSELF. The prior verdict at 0c09fe8e2ca6 was recorded by `aida drain reviewer`, which has exited, and its handshake summary says "both binding round-3 rework requirements remain missing" WITHOUT SAYING WHAT THEY ARE - the findings were lost to BUG-1539's clobber. I recovered them from the GitHub comment at 2026-09-20T23:18, which is the only durable copy. This verdict quotes both requirements in full above so the next reader of the handshake file does not have to do that archaeology, and I saved the previous record before recording this one.
subject: #1974 (STORY-1350/1357): both binding round-3 requirements SATISFIED; one new finding the rework introduced - the absence message hard-codes the marker the commit exists to couple
